Five Women Who Ruled the World

Every queen has two stories — the one history recorded, and the one it tried to hide. We tell both. Tap any queen to jump straight to her full story below — every story is published here in full, in three languages.

Queen No. 1 — Egypt

Cleopatra

69 – 30 BC · The Last Pharaoh

History remembers her beauty. It forgets that she spoke nine languages, wrote medical treatises, and negotiated with Rome as an equal when no other ruler dared. She was not Egypt's ornament — she was Egypt's sharpest mind.

Read her full story

Elizabeth I

1533 – 1603 · England

Declared illegitimate, imprisoned by her own sister — then reigned 45 years and defeated the Spanish Armada. The Virgin Queen who married a kingdom instead of a man.

Read her story →

Catherine the Great

1729 – 1796 · Russia

A minor German princess who arrived in Russia with nothing, learned the language, and took the throne itself. She expanded an empire and corresponded with Voltaire.

Read her story →

Queen Victoria

1819 – 1901 · Britain

Queen at eighteen, on the throne for 63 years — longer than any British monarch before her. An era of railways, industry and empire still carries her name.

Read her story →

Mary, Queen of Scots

1542 – 1587 · Scotland

Queen at six days old. Widowed at eighteen, imprisoned for nineteen years, and brave to the very scaffold — her life reads like a novel no writer would dare invent.

Read her story →
Season Two · 第二季 · 第二季

Nefertiti

c. 1370 – 1330 BC · Egypt

Everyone knows her face — the bust in Berlin is one of the most reproduced in the world. Then, mid-reign, her name simply stops. No tomb, no body, no goodbye.

Read her story →

Wu Zetian

624 – 705 · China

She entered the palace at fourteen as a low-ranking concubine — and became the only woman in Chinese history to take the throne as emperor, in her own name.

Read her story →

Isabella I

1451 – 1504 · Spain

Columbus got the statues. She got the decision every adviser in the room opposed — the signature that sent three ships west and changed the map of the world.

Read her story →

Rani Lakshmibai

1828 – 1858 · India

Her kingdom was taken not by an army but by a clause. She fought back with petitions for years — and when every door closed, she rode to war herself.

Read her story →

Maria Theresa

1717 – 1780 · Austria

At twenty-three she inherited a throne every signed promise said was safe. The promises lasted about as long as her father's funeral. She held it for forty years.

Read her story →

Queen No. 1 — Egypt

Cleopatra — The Queen Who Spoke Nine Languages

克利奥帕特拉——会说九种语言的女王

克麗奧佩特拉——會說九種語言的女王

69 – 30 BC · The Last Pharaoh

I was not born to be a pretty face in someone else's story. I was born to keep a kingdom alive.

Everyone remembers the eyeliner. Almost no one remembers the languages. I spoke nine — Egyptian, Greek, Latin, and six more — and I was the first Ptolemy in three hundred years who bothered to learn the language of the people I ruled. My ancestors spoke Greek to Greeks and let Egypt translate itself. I walked into the room and spoke to Egypt in Egyptian.

That is the part they leave out of the love story. Rome did not come for me because I was beautiful. Rome came because Egypt fed Rome, and I was the one holding the grain, the gold, and the fleet. Antony needed me the way a general needs a supply line. Octavian feared me the way an emperor fears a rival who can pay for her own war.

I lost, in the end. But look at what I kept for twenty-one years: a kingdom that was supposed to be swallowed, a language that was supposed to stay foreign, and a name that, two thousand years later, still opens every room.

And I did more than survive Rome. With the astronomer Sosigenes I helped reshape the calendar Egypt lived by — the work that fed into the Julian calendar the world used for over a thousand years. I built at Dendera, endowed temples, and kept Alexandria's scholars fed and arguing. A queen who funds astronomers is not decorating history. She is writing it.

A modern parallel: the founder who learns the language of her own team instead of making the team learn hers. Power is not the crown. Power is being understood without a translator.

我生来不是为了做别人故事里的漂亮脸蛋，我生来是为了让一个王国活下去。

人人都记得我的眼线，几乎没人记得我的语言。我会说九种语言——埃及语、希腊语、拉丁语，还有六种——我是三百年来第一个愿意学自己人民语言的托勒密王。我的祖先只对希腊人说希腊语，让埃及自己去翻译。我走进房间，直接用埃及语和埃及说话。

这才是爱情故事里被删掉的部分。罗马不是因为我漂亮才来的，罗马来是因为埃及养活了罗马，而粮食、黄金和舰队都在我手里。安东尼需要我，就像将军需要补给线；屋大维怕我，就像皇帝怕一个能自己出钱打仗的对手。

最后我输了。但看看我守了二十一年的是什么：一个本该被吞掉的王国，一种本该一直陌生的语言，和一个两千年后仍能打开每一扇门的名字。

而且我做的不只是熬过罗马。我和天文学家索西琴尼一起改了埃及用的历法——那份工作后来汇入了儒略历，全世界用了一千多年。我在丹德拉建神庙、资助寺院，让亚历山大城的学者有饭吃、有架吵。一个出钱养天文学家的女王，不是在装饰历史，她是在书写历史。

今天的对照：那个学会自己团队语言的创始人，而不是让团队来学她的语言。权力不是王冠，权力是不用翻译就能被听懂。

我生來不是為了做別人故事裡的漂亮臉蛋，我生來是為了讓一個王國活下去。

人人都記得我的眼線，幾乎沒人記得我的語言。我會說九種語言——埃及語、希臘語、拉丁語，還有六種——我是三百年來第一個願意學自己人民語言的托勒密王。我的祖先只對希臘人說希臘語，讓埃及自己去翻譯。我走進房間，直接用埃及語和埃及說話。

這才是愛情故事裡被刪掉的部分。羅馬不是因為我漂亮才來的，羅馬來是因為埃及養活了羅馬，而糧食、黃金和艦隊都在我手裡。安東尼需要我，就像將軍需要補給線；屋大維怕我，就像皇帝怕一個能自己出錢打仗的對手。

最後我輸了。但看看我守了二十一年的是什麼：一個本該被吞掉的王國，一種本該一直陌生的語言，和一個兩千年後仍能打開每一扇門的名字。

而且我做的不只是熬過羅馬。我和天文學家索西琴尼一起改了埃及用的曆法——那份工作後來匯入了儒略曆，全世界用了一千多年。我在丹德拉建神廟、資助寺院，讓亞歷山大城的學者有飯吃、有架吵。一個出錢養天文學家的女王，不是在裝飾歷史，她是在書寫歷史。

今天的對照：那個學會自己團隊語言的創始人，而不是讓團隊來學她的語言。權力不是王冠，權力是不用翻譯就能被聽懂。

Queen No. 2 — England

Elizabeth I — The Princess Who Was Written Off

伊丽莎白一世——被除名的公主

伊莉莎白一世——被除名的公主

1533 – 1603 · England

I was written off before I could write my own name. Declared a bastard at two, a prisoner in my teens, a woman no one expected to survive the year — let alone rule for forty-five of them.

They kept a file on me: too clever, too stubborn, too much my father's daughter and too much my mother's. My mother was executed when I was two. My sister locked me in the Tower. Every court in Europe took bets on how fast I would fall, and every one of them lost the bet.

So I learned the one skill that kept me alive: I made waiting look like weakness, and weakness look like patience. I let suitors wait. I let ambassadors wait. I let Spain wait. While they waited, I built a navy, a church, and a country that could pay its own bills.

People call me the Virgin Queen, as if the most interesting thing about me was what I did not do. The most interesting thing is what I did do: I never married, so no king could own my crown; I never named an heir, so no faction could own my future. I kept the pen in my own hand for forty-five years.

In August 1588, with the Spanish Armada in the Channel, I rode to Tilbury and told my soldiers I had "the heart and stomach of a king". The Armada broke — on English ships, Protestant winds, and a queen who refused to blink. The reign that followed gave England stability, a golden age of theatre and poetry, and a simple lesson courts kept relearning: never mistake a patient woman for a weak one.

A modern parallel: the woman who is counted out in the meeting, and quietly outlasts every man who counted her out. Being written off is not the end of the story. It is the first page.

我还没学会写自己的名字，就已经被一笔勾销了。两岁被宣布为私生女，十几岁就成了阶下囚，一个没人指望她能活过当年的女人——更别说统治四十五年。

他们给我建了个档案：太聪明，太倔，太像我父亲，也太像我母亲。我母亲在我两岁时被处死，我姐姐把我关进伦敦塔。欧洲每个宫廷都在打赌我多快会倒下，每一个赌局他们都输了。

所以我学会了让我活下来的本事：把等待装成软弱，把软弱装成耐心。我让求婚者等，让大使等，让西班牙等。他们等着的时候，我建了一支海军、一座教堂、一个能自己付账的国家。

人们叫我童贞女王，好像我最有意思的事是我没做什么。我最有意思的事是我做了什么：我一辈子没结婚，所以没有国王能拥有我的王冠；我一辈子没指定继承人，所以没有派系能拥有我的未来。王冠的笔，我自己握了四十五年。

1588年8月，西班牙无敌舰队压进英吉利海峡，我骑马到蒂尔伯里，对士兵们说，我有"国王的心和国王的胆"。无敌舰队碎了——碎在英国的战船上、新教的风向上，和一个拒绝眨眼的女王手里。之后的统治给了英格兰稳定，给了戏剧与诗歌的黄金时代，也给了一个宫廷们一再重新学习的教训：永远别把有耐心的女人当成软弱的女人。

今天的对照：那个在会议上被看扁的女人，悄悄熬过了每一个看扁她的男人。被一笔勾销不是故事的结尾，那是第一页。

我還沒學會寫自己的名字，就已經被一筆勾銷了。兩歲被宣布為私生女，十幾歲就成了階下囚，一個沒人指望她能活過當年的女人——更別說統治四十五年。

他們給我建了個檔案：太聰明，太倔，太像我父親，也太像我母親。我母親在我兩歲時被處死，我姐姐把我關進倫敦塔。歐洲每個宮廷都在打賭我多快會倒下，每一個賭局他們都輸了。

所以我學會了讓我活下來的本事：把等待裝成軟弱，把軟弱裝成耐心。我讓求婚者等，讓大使等，讓西班牙等。他們等著的時候，我建了一支海軍、一座教堂、一個能自己付帳的國家。

人們叫我童貞女王，好像我最有意思的事是我沒做什麼。我最有意思的事是我做了什麼：我一輩子沒結婚，所以沒有國王能擁有我的王冠；我一輩子沒指定繼承人，所以沒有派系能擁有我的未來。王冠的筆，我自己握了四十五年。

1588年8月，西班牙無敵艦隊壓進英吉利海峽，我騎馬到蒂爾伯里，對士兵們說，我有「國王的心和國王的膽」。無敵艦隊碎了——碎在英國的戰船上、新教的風向上，和一個拒絕眨眼的女王手裡。之後的統治給了英格蘭穩定，給了戲劇與詩歌的黃金時代，也給了一個宮廷們一再重新學習的教訓：永遠別把有耐心的女人當成軟弱的女人。

今天的對照：那個在會議上被看扁的女人，悄悄熬過了每一個看扁她的男人。被一筆勾銷不是故事的結尾，那是第一頁。

Queen No. 3 — Russia

Catherine the Great — The Foreign Bride Who Took an Empire

叶卡捷琳娜大帝——嫁过来的外国新娘

葉卡捷琳娜大帝——嫁過來的外國新娘

1729 – 1796 · Russia

I arrived in Russia as a fifteen-year-old German princess with a new name, a new religion, and no friends. The court laughed at my accent. My husband — the future emperor — ignored me, then humiliated me. The plan, as far as anyone could see, was for me to produce an heir and disappear quietly into the background.

I had a different plan. I learned Russian until I dreamed in it. I read Voltaire in French and the law in Russian. I made friends with the guards, the priests, and the generals — the people who actually hold a country together — while my husband made enemies of all of them.

When the moment came, I did not ask for the throne. I rode out at the head of the guards, in a uniform, and took it. I ruled for thirty-four years, expanded the empire to the Black Sea, and wrote to the philosophers of Europe as an equal. The foreign bride became the most Russian ruler Russia ever had.

People remember the scandals, because scandals are easier to tell than statecraft. What I actually did was harder: I out-learned, out-waited, and out-worked everyone who was born to the job, and I never once let them see me rush.

And I governed like I had studied. In 1767 I wrote my Instruction — a great legal code drawn from the thinkers of the Enlightenment — and summoned deputies from across the empire to debate it. In 1768, when smallpox terrified Russia, I had myself inoculated first, in public, so the country would follow. I founded the Hermitage collection, took Crimea in 1783, and left Russia larger, richer and harder to ignore than I found it.

A modern parallel: the outsider hired into a company that does not speak her language, who learns the language, learns the room, and ends up running the room. You do not need to be born inside. You need to be the one who does the reading.

我十五岁来到俄国，是个德国小公主，带着新名字、新宗教，没有一个朋友。宫廷笑我的口音，我丈夫——未来的皇帝——不理我，后来还羞辱我。在所有人看来，我的任务就是生个继承人，然后悄悄退到幕后。

我有别的计划。我学俄语学到做梦都说俄语，用法语读伏尔泰，用俄语读法律。我和卫兵、神父、将军们交朋友——那些真正撑起一个国家的人——而我丈夫把他们全得罪光了。

时机到了，我没有请求王位，我穿着军装骑在卫兵前面，自己拿下了它。我统治了三十四年，把帝国扩到黑海，和欧洲的哲学家平起平坐地通信。那个外国新娘，成了俄国最俄国的统治者。

人们记得那些丑闻，因为丑闻比治国好讲。我真正做的事更难：我比所有生来就该干这份工作的人学得更多、等得更久、干得更多，而且一次也没让他们看出来我着急。

而且我治国的方式，就像我读书的方式一样认真。1767年，我写下《训谕》——一部取材于启蒙思想家的法典草案——还召集帝国各地的代表来讨论它。1768年，天花吓坏了整个俄国，我第一个当众接种，让全国跟着做。我创办了冬宫的收藏，1783年拿下克里米亚，留下的俄国比我接手时更大、更富、更让人无法忽视。

今天的对照：那个被招进一家不说她语言的公司的外来者，学会了语言，学会了看房间，最后成了掌管房间的人。你不需要生在里面，你只需要是那个做功课的人。

我十五歲來到俄國，是個德國小公主，帶著新名字、新宗教，沒有一個朋友。宮廷笑我的口音，我丈夫——未來的皇帝——不理我，後來還羞辱我。在所有人看來，我的任務就是生個繼承人，然後悄悄退到幕後。

我有別的計劃。我學俄語學到做夢都說俄語，用法語讀伏爾泰，用俄語讀法律。我和衛兵、神父、將軍們交朋友——那些真正撐起一個國家的人——而我丈夫把他們全得罪光了。

時機到了，我沒有請求王位，我穿著軍裝騎在衛兵前面，自己拿下了它。我統治了三十四年，把帝國擴到黑海，和歐洲的哲學家平起平坐地通信。那個外國新娘，成了俄國最俄國的統治者。

人們記得那些醜聞，因為醜聞比治國好講。我真正做的事更難：我比所有生來就該幹這份工作的人學得更多、等得更久、幹得更多，而且一次也沒讓他們看出來我著急。

而且我治國的方式，就像我讀書的方式一樣認真。1767年，我寫下《訓諭》——一部取材於啟蒙思想家的法典草案——還召集帝國各地的代表來討論它。1768年，天花嚇壞了整個俄國，我第一個當眾接種，讓全國跟著做。我創辦了冬宮的收藏，1783年拿下克里米亞，留下的俄國比我接手時更大、更富、更讓人無法忽視。

今天的對照：那個被招進一家不說她語言的公司的外來者，學會了語言，學會了看房間，最後成了掌管房間的人。你不需要生在裡面，你只需要是那個做功課的人。

Queen No. 4 — Britain

Queen Victoria — The Teenager Who Inherited the World

维多利亚女王——十八岁继承世界的少女

維多利亞女王——十八歲繼承世界的少女

1819 – 1901 · Britain

I was eighteen when the world landed in my lap. Eighteen, five feet tall, and suddenly the queen of the largest empire the world had ever seen. The men around the throne had spent my whole childhood planning how to rule through me. They had not planned on me ruling at all.

Here is what they did not understand: I had spent my childhood in a room with rules. My mother and her adviser ran my life on a system — the Kensington System — that told me when to eat, when to sleep, who I could talk to. I was watched so closely I could barely breathe. So by eighteen, I already knew exactly what a cage looked like, and I had no intention of living in another one.

My first act as queen was a small one, and it told the whole story: I asked for my bed to be moved out of my mother's room. One bed, one room, one line drawn. After that, I chose my own husband, kept my own hours, and ran my own government — sixty-three years of it, the longest reign in British history until my great-great-granddaughter passed it.

They called me the Grandmother of Europe, because my children and grandchildren married into nearly every throne on the continent. That was not an accident. That was strategy, done in a black dress, at a desk, one letter at a time.

The world changed under my desk. In 1851 the Great Exhibition filled London's Crystal Palace with the machines of a new age — six million visitors came to see the future, and my husband Albert helped make it happen. When he died in 1861 I wore black for the rest of my life, but I never stopped working: dispatches, ministers, nine children married across Europe. In 1876 I became Empress of India; in 1897 my Diamond Jubilee marked sixty years — a reign that began with horse-drawn coaches and ended with telegrams, trains and photographs.

A modern parallel: the young woman who is handed a job everyone assumes she cannot do, and quietly turns it into the longest run in the room. She does not need to be loud. She needs to be the one still standing at the end.

我十八岁那年，世界落到了我手里。十八岁，身高一米五，突然成了世界上有史以来最大帝国的女王。王座周围的男人们花了我整个童年，计划着怎么通过我来统治。他们根本没计划过让我自己统治。

他们没明白的是：我的童年是在一间有规矩的房间里过的。我母亲和她的顾问用一套制度——肯辛顿制度——管着我的生活，什么时候吃饭，什么时候睡觉，能和谁说话。我被看得死死的，几乎喘不过气。所以到十八岁，我已经很清楚笼子长什么样了，我没打算再住进另一个笼子。

我当女王后的第一个举动很小，却说明了一切：我要求把我的床搬出我母亲的房间。一张床，一个房间，一条线。从那以后，我自己选丈夫，自己安排时间，自己管理政府——六十三年，英国历史上最长的统治，直到我的玄孙女才超过它。

人们叫我欧洲的祖母，因为我的子女和孙辈嫁进了欧洲几乎每一个王位。那不是巧合，那是策略，穿着黑裙子，坐在书桌前，一封信一封信写出来的。

世界在我书桌底下变了样。1851年，万国博览会把新时代的机器装满了伦敦的水晶宫——六百万人来看未来，我的丈夫阿尔伯特是幕后推手之一。1861年他去世后，我终生穿黑，但从未停工：公文、大臣、九个嫁到欧洲各地的孩子。1876年，我成为印度女皇；1897年钻石禧，六十年——一段始于马车、终于电报、火车和照片的统治。

今天的对照：那个接手了一份人人都以为她做不了的工作的年轻女人，悄悄把它做成了全场最长的一任。她不需要大声，她只需要在最后还站着。

我十八歲那年，世界落到了我手裡。十八歲，身高一米五，突然成了世界上有史以來最大帝國的女王。王座周圍的男人們花了我整個童年，計劃著怎麼通過我來統治。他們根本沒計劃過讓我自己統治。

他們沒明白的是：我的童年是在一間有規矩的房間裡過的。我母親和她的顧問用一套制度——肯辛頓制度——管著我的生活，什麼時候吃飯，什麼時候睡覺，能和誰說話。我被看得死死的，幾乎喘不過氣。所以到十八歲，我已經很清楚籠子長什麼樣了，我沒打算再住進另一個籠子。

我當女王後的第一個舉動很小，卻說明了一切：我要求把我的床搬出我母親的房間。一張床，一個房間，一條線。從那以後，我自己選丈夫，自己安排時間，自己管理政府——六十三年，英國歷史上最長的統治，直到我的玄孫女才超過它。

人們叫我歐洲的祖母，因為我的子女和孫輩嫁進了歐洲幾乎每一個王位。那不是巧合，那是策略，穿著黑裙子，坐在書桌前，一封信一封信寫出來的。

世界在我書桌底下變了樣。1851年，萬國博覽會把新時代的機器裝滿了倫敦的水晶宮——六百萬人來看未來，我的丈夫阿爾伯特是幕後推手之一。1861年他去世後，我終生穿黑，但從未停工：公文、大臣、九個嫁到歐洲各地的孩子。1876年，我成為印度女皇；1897年鑽石禧，六十年——一段始於馬車、終於電報、火車和照片的統治。

今天的對照：那個接手了一份人人都以為她做不了的工作的年輕女人，悄悄把它做成了全場最長的一任。她不需要大聲，她只需要在最後還站著。

← Catherine the Great Next: Mary, Queen of Scots →
Queen No. 5 — Scotland

Mary, Queen of Scots — The Queen Crowned at Six Days Old

玛丽女王——出生六天就登基的女王

瑪麗女王——出生六天就登基的女王

1542 – 1587 · Scotland

I was crowned queen at six days old. Six days. I had not yet learned to open my eyes, and already a crown was being fitted to a head that could not hold it up.

That is the story of my life in one sentence: too much, too soon, and no one ever asked me what I wanted. I was a child queen, a child bride, a child widow — married at fifteen, widowed at seventeen, a queen in two countries and at home in neither.

They say I was beautiful, and that my beauty was my ruin. It was not my beauty. It was my choices, made in a world that gave a woman no good ones. I married for love and it killed my husband's reputation. I married for safety and it killed my husband. I fled to my cousin Elizabeth for protection, and she locked me up for nineteen years — then signed the paper that took my head.

Nineteen years in a room, and I never stopped writing letters. Letters to kings, to popes, to anyone who might remember I existed. My handwriting was my last kingdom, and I ruled it to the end.

Here is the part they do not put on the postcards: I lost the crown, the country, and my life — but I never lost my name. Four hundred years later, people still argue about me as if I were alive. That is a kind of winning, too.

On the morning of my execution at Fotheringhay in February 1587, I wore crimson — the colour of martyrdom — under my black dress, so that when the black came off, the room would remember. I was forty-four. My son James, raised a Protestant in Scotland without me, went on to inherit Elizabeth's throne as well, joining the two crowns I could never hold together in life. Even my ending argued my case: a queen, executed by another queen who never dared meet her face to face.

A modern parallel: the woman who is given everything at the start and nothing that lasts, and still refuses to disappear quietly. She keeps writing. She keeps her name.

我出生六天就登基了。六天，我还没学会睁开眼睛，王冠就已经戴到了一个抬不起头的脑袋上。

这就是我一生的写照，一句话：太多，太早，从来没人问过我想要什么。我是孩童女王、孩童新娘、孩童寡妇——十五岁结婚，十七岁守寡，两个国家的女王，哪个国家都不是我的家。

人们说我漂亮，说我的美貌毁了我。毁了我的不是美貌，是我的选择，在一个不给女人好选择的世界里做的选择。我为爱结婚，毁了我丈夫的名声；我为安全结婚，毁了我丈夫的命；我逃到表姐伊丽莎白那里寻求保护，她把我关了十九年——然后签下了砍我头的那张纸。

十九年关在一个房间里，我从来没停过写信。写给国王，写给教皇，写给任何可能还记得我存在的人。我的笔迹是我最后的王国，我统治它直到最后。

明信片上不会写的那部分是：我丢了王冠、国家和性命——但我从来没丢掉我的名字。四百年后，人们还在争论我，好像我还活着。这也是一种赢。

1587年2月，在福瑟林盖行刑的那个早晨，我在黑裙子里面穿了深红——殉道的颜色——等黑裙脱下，整个房间都会记住。我那年四十四岁。我的儿子詹姆斯，在苏格兰被按新教养大、没在我身边长大，后来继承了伊丽莎白的王位，把我一生都合不到一起的两顶王冠合到了一起。就连我的结局都在替我辩护：一个女王，被另一个从不敢与她当面对质的女王处死。

今天的对照：那个一开始得到了一切、却什么都没能留住的女人，仍然拒绝悄悄消失。她继续写，她守住自己的名字。

我出生六天就登基了。六天，我還沒學會睜開眼睛，王冠就已經戴到了一個抬不起頭的腦袋上。

這就是我一生的寫照，一句話：太多，太早，從來沒人問過我想要什麼。我是孩童女王、孩童新娘、孩童寡婦——十五歲結婚，十七歲守寡，兩個國家的女王，哪個國家都不是我的家。

人們說我漂亮，說我的美貌毀了我。毀了我的不是美貌，是我的選擇，在一個不給女人好選擇的世界裡做的選擇。我為愛結婚，毀了我丈夫的名聲；我為安全結婚，毀了我丈夫的命；我逃到表姐伊莉莎白那裡尋求保護，她把我關了十九年——然後簽下了砍我頭的那張紙。

十九年關在一個房間裡，我從來沒停過寫信。寫給國王，寫給教皇，寫給任何可能還記得我存在的人。我的筆跡是我最後的王國，我統治它直到最後。

明信片上不會寫的那部分是：我丟了王冠、國家和性命——但我從來沒丟掉我的名字。四百年後，人們還在爭論我，好像我還活著。這也是一種贏。

1587年2月，在福瑟林蓋行刑的那個早晨，我在黑裙子裡面穿了深紅——殉道的顏色——等黑裙脫下，整個房間都會記住。我那年四十四歲。我的兒子詹姆斯，在蘇格蘭被按新教養大、沒在我身邊長大，後來繼承了伊莉莎白的王位，把我一生都合不到一起的兩頂王冠合到了一起。就連我的結局都在替我辯護：一個女王，被另一個從不敢與她當面對質的女王處死。

今天的對照：那個一開始得到了一切、卻什麼都沒能留住的女人，仍然拒絕悄悄消失。她繼續寫，她守住自己的名字。

Season Two — Five More Queens

Five more queens join the collection — an Egyptian icon who vanished from the record, China's only female emperor, the queen who signed a new world into being, a warrior who first fought with paperwork, and a mother who rebuilt an empire. All five stories are published here in full, in three languages.

Language 语言 語言
Queen No. 6 — Egypt

Nefertiti — The Queen Who Vanished

尼菲提提——消失的女王

尼菲提提——消失的女王

c. 1370 – 1330 BC · The Queen Who Vanished

I did not disappear because I was unimportant. I disappeared because I mattered too much to erase cleanly.

Everyone knows my face. A painted bust, made in the workshop of the sculptor Thutmose more than three thousand years ago, found in 1912 and now in Berlin — it is one of the most reproduced faces in the world. People copy the eyeliner, the long neck, the tall blue crown. Almost no one asks what the woman wearing them actually did.

I was the Great Royal Wife of Akhenaten, and together we tried to change everything: one god instead of many, a new capital built from nothing at Amarna, art that showed a royal family eating, playing, holding their children — a king and queen you could almost touch. For a few years, I was not standing behind the throne. I was standing beside it, in the carvings, in the ceremonies, in the decisions.

Then, around the twelfth year of his reign, my name stops. No tomb found, no body identified for certain, no record that says where I went. Some scholars think I ruled on after him under another name. That is a theory, not a fact — and the honest part is this: we do not know. What we know is that a woman who helped run an empire can vanish from the record, and still be recognised by her face three thousand years later.

What survived me is stranger than any tomb. My bust was buried in the rubble of Thutmose's workshop when Amarna was abandoned, and it slept there for more than three thousand years, until a German excavation team led by Ludwig Borchardt uncovered it in December 1912. Within a generation, my face was on magazine covers and in art classrooms everywhere — a queen with no confirmed grave became the most recognisable woman of the ancient world. The record lost my name for a while. It never lost my face.

A modern parallel: the founder whose face is on every slide and whose name is missing from every decision record. Being seen is not the same as being remembered for what you did — so write your own record while you still can.

我消失，不是因为我不重要，是因为我太重要了，抹都抹不干净。

全世界都认得我的脸。那尊彩绘半身像，是三千多年前雕刻家图特摩斯工坊里的作品，1912 年出土，现在放在柏林，是世界上被复制最多的脸之一。人人都学我的眼线、长脖子、高高的蓝色王冠，几乎没人问：戴着它们的那个女人，到底做过什么。

我是法老阿肯那顿的大王后。我们一起想把一切都改了：只信一个神，在阿玛纳从零建一座新都，画里的王室一家吃饭、玩耍、抱孩子——一个你几乎能摸到的国王和王后。有几年，我不是站在王座后面，我是站在王座旁边，刻在石壁上、站在仪式里、坐在决定里。

然后，在他统治的第十二年左右，我的名字停了。没有找到陵墓，没有确认身份的遗体，没有记录说我去了哪里。有学者认为我后来换了个名字继续统治，那只是推测，不是定论。老实说就是：我们不知道。我们知道的是，一个帮着管过帝国的人，可以从记录里消失，而她的脸三千年后还被人认得。

比任何陵墓都更离奇地活下来的，是我的半身像。阿玛纳被废弃时，它埋在图特摩斯工坊的废墟里，一睡三千多年，直到1912年12月，路德维希·博尔夏特带领的德国考古队把它挖出来。不过一代人的时间，我的脸就登上了杂志封面和各地的美术课堂——一个连墓地都没有确认的女王，成了古代世界最广为人知的女人。记录一度弄丢了我的名字，却从没弄丢我的脸。

今天的对照：那个脸在每张幻灯片上、名字却不在任何决定记录里的创始人。被人看见，不等于被人记住你做过什么——趁还来得及，自己写下自己的记录。

我消失，不是因為我不重要，是因為我太重要了，抹都抹不乾淨。

全世界都認得我的臉。那尊彩繪半身像，是三千多年前雕刻家圖特摩斯工坊裡的作品，1912 年出土，現在放在柏林，是世界上被複製最多的臉之一。人人都學我的眼線、長脖子、高高的藍色王冠，幾乎沒人問：戴著它們的那個女人，到底做過什麼。

我是法老阿肯那頓的大王后。我們一起想把一切都改了：只信一個神，在阿瑪納從零建一座新都，畫裡的王室一家吃飯、玩耍、抱孩子——一個你幾乎能摸到的國王和王后。有幾年，我不是站在王座後面，我是站在王座旁邊，刻在石壁上、站在儀式裡、坐在決定裡。

然後，在他統治的第十二年左右，我的名字停了。沒有找到陵墓，沒有確認身份的遺體，沒有記錄說我去了哪裡。有學者認為我後來換了個名字繼續統治，那只是推測，不是定論。老實說就是：我們不知道。我們知道的是，一個幫著管過帝國的人，可以從記錄裡消失，而她的臉三千年後還被人認得。

比任何陵墓都更離奇地活下來的，是我的半身像。阿瑪納被廢棄時，它埋在圖特摩斯工坊的廢墟裡，一睡三千多年，直到1912年12月，路德維希·博爾夏特帶領的德國考古隊把它挖出來。不過一代人的時間，我的臉就登上了雜誌封面和各地的美術課堂——一個連墓地都沒有確認的女王，成了古代世界最廣為人知的女人。記錄一度弄丟了我的名字，卻從沒弄丟我的臉。

今天的對照：那個臉在每張幻燈片上、名字卻不在任何決定記錄裡的創始人。被人看見，不等於被人記住你做過什麼——趁還來得及，自己寫下自己的記錄。

Queen No. 7 — China

Wu Zetian — The Empress Who Ruled as Emperor

武则天——自己登基的女皇帝

武則天——自己登基的女皇帝

624 – 705 · The Empress Who Ruled as Emperor

I was not born to be a palace concubine; I was born to be the only woman in Chinese history to sit on an emperor's throne.

At fourteen I entered Emperor Taizong's palace as a low-ranking concubine. When he died in 649, I had no children, so I was sent to a Buddhist convent — the quiet ending the court gave women like me. It was supposed to be the end of my story.

Emperor Gaozong brought me back. In 655 I was crowned empress, and as his health failed, more and more of the empire's business crossed my desk. People called me his wife. The paperwork called me something else.

In 690 I founded my own dynasty, Zhou, and took the throne as emperor — in my own name, not as a husband's wife or a son's regent. I widened the imperial examinations, so a man could rise by what he knew, not only by who his father was. I ruled fifteen years. In 705, at eighty-one, I gave up the throne, and died the same year. At my tomb in Qianling stands a stele with no words on it at all. Historians still argue about why. Let them.

I also spent power on things that outlasted me. I raised the weight of the examinations, added military exams, and let talent argue with birth. I poured patronage into Buddhism — the great Vairocana Buddha at the Longmen Grottoes, carved in my era, is said to carry my features. And I left that wordless stele at Qianling on purpose or not, it has done its work: fourteen centuries later, people are still standing in front of it, arguing about me. Silence, it turns out, can be the loudest inscription.

A modern parallel: the assistant who learns every desk in the office because no one will teach her the top one. Every step of my climb had a sign on it that said: not for you. I stopped asking the signs. I learned the machine from the bottom, waited out everyone who owned it, and in the end the signature on the documents was mine.

我不是生来要做宫里的妃子的，我是生来要成为中国历史上唯一一个坐上皇帝宝座的女人的。

十四岁那年，我进了太宗的宫里，做一个低等妃子。649年太宗去世，我没有孩子，就被送进寺院——那是宫廷给我们这种女人安排的安静结局。我的故事，本该在那里结束。

高宗把我接了回来。655年，我做了皇后；他身体一天不如一天，越来越多的国事开始过我的手。人们叫我他的妻子，可公文上写的，是另一个身份。

690年，我立了自己的朝代——周，以我自己的名义登基做皇帝，不是谁的妻子，也不是谁的摄政。我扩大了科举，让人凭本事升官，而不是凭他爹是谁。我做了十五年皇帝。705年，我八十一岁，交出皇位，同年去世。乾陵前立着我的碑，上面一个字都没有。史学家们到今天还在争论为什么。就让他们争吧。

我也把权力花在比我活得更久的事情上。我加重了科举的分量，增设武举，让才能和出身掰手腕。我大力扶持佛教——龙门石窟那尊卢舍那大佛，就是我那个时代凿的，传说脸是照着我的模样刻的。至于乾陵前那块无字碑，不管我是有意还是无意，它已经起了作用：一千四百年后，人们还站在它面前争论我。原来沉默，可以是最响亮的碑文。

今天的对照：那位把办公室里每一张桌子都学会了的助理，因为没有人肯教她最高的那一张。我往上走的每一步，都挂着一块牌子，写着：不适合你。我不再去问那些牌子了。我从最底层学会这台机器怎么转，把占着位置的人一个一个熬过去——最后，文件上的签名，是我的。

我不是生來要做宮裡的妃子的，我是生來要成為中國歷史上唯一一個坐上皇帝寶座的女人的。

十四歲那年，我進了太宗的宮裡，做一個低等妃子。649年太宗去世，我沒有孩子，就被送進寺院——那是宮廷給我們這種女人安排的安靜結局。我的故事，本該在那裡結束。

高宗把我接了回來。655年，我做了皇后；他身體一天不如一天，越來越多的國事開始過我的手。人們叫我他的妻子，可公文上寫的，是另一個身分。

690年，我立了自己的朝代——周，以我自己的名義登基做皇帝，不是誰的妻子，也不是誰的攝政。我擴大了科舉，讓人憑本事升官，而不是憑他爹是誰。我做了十五年皇帝。705年，我八十一歲，交出皇位，同年去世。乾陵前立著我的碑，上面一個字都沒有。史學家們到今天還在爭論為什麼。就讓他們爭吧。

我也把權力花在比我活得更久的事情上。我加重了科舉的分量，增設武舉，讓才能和出身掰手腕。我大力扶持佛教——龍門石窟那尊盧舍那大佛，就是我那個時代鑿的，傳說臉是照著我的模樣刻的。至於乾陵前那塊無字碑，不管我是有意還是無意，它已經起了作用：一千四百年後，人們還站在它面前爭論我。原來沉默，可以是最響亮的碑文。

今天的對照：那位把辦公室裡每一張桌子都學會了的助理，因為沒有人肯教她最高的那一張。我往上走的每一步，都掛著一塊牌子，寫著：不適合你。我不再去問那些牌子了。我從最底層學會這台機器怎麼轉，把占著位置的人一個一個熬過去——最後，文件上的簽名，是我的。

Queen No. 8 — Spain

Isabella I — The Queen Who Financed a New World

伊莎贝拉一世——资助新大陆的女王

伊莎貝拉一世——資助新大陸的女王

1451 – 1504 · The Queen Who Financed a New World

Everyone remembers the sailor. Almost no one remembers the woman who paid for the ships. Columbus got the statues. I got the decision — the one every adviser in the room was against.

I took the throne of Castile in 1474, and my niece Juana's side did not accept it. For four years I fought a civil war for a crown that was already supposed to be mine. I had married Ferdinand of Aragon in 1469 — a partner, yes, but in Castile the crown, the kingdom and the signature stayed mine.

In January 1492 I completed the conquest of Granada, the last Muslim kingdom in Spain. That same year Columbus came back with his plan to sail west to Asia. He had been asking courts for years. My advisers said no. I said yes, and signed. He sailed in August, and in October he reached a world none of us had on our maps. People say I pawned my jewels to pay for it. That is a story. What I paid with was a signature no one else would give.

Here is the part they leave out. When Columbus brought enslaved people from those new lands to be sold in Spain, I was furious. I ordered them freed and sent home. The people across the ocean were my subjects, I said — not merchandise. A signature can open a world. It also makes you answerable for what sails back.

Honesty demands the hard edge too. The same year I finished the conquest of Granada, I signed the Alhambra Decree, expelling Spain's Jews, and the Inquisition I had authorised in 1478 pursued heresy with a cruelty history has not forgiven. I also founded hospitals, encouraged printing, and standardised the laws of a newly united Spain. A full record holds all of it at once: the signature that opened a world, and the signatures that closed doors on my own people. That is what it means to tell a life whole.

A modern parallel: the woman whose "yes" is the one that counts. Everyone around her has a reason to say no — too risky, too new, too strange. Her job is not just to sign. It is to stay responsible after she signs, especially for the people with the least power in the room. That is what a signature is for.

大家都记得那个水手，几乎没人记得出钱买船的女人。哥伦布得到了雕像，我得到的是那个决定——房间里每一个顾问都反对的决定。

1474年，我登上了卡斯蒂利亚的王位，可我的侄女胡安娜一方不认。接下来四年，我为这顶本该属于我的王冠打了一场内战。1469年，我嫁给了阿拉贡的费尔南多——是伙伴，没错；但在卡斯蒂利亚，王冠、王国和签名，都留在我手里。

1492年1月，我完成了对格拉纳达的征服，西班牙最后一个穆斯林王国就此结束。同一年，哥伦布带着向西航行去亚洲的计划又来了。他多年来一直在各国宫廷请求资助。我的顾问说不行，我说行，签了字。他8月起航，10月抵达了一个谁的地图上都没有的世界。有人说我典当了珠宝来付这笔钱。那是传说。我真正付出的，是一份别人都不肯给的签名。

他们不讲的那一段是这样的：哥伦布把从新大陆掳来的人当奴隶带回西班牙贩卖时，我大发雷霆。我下令放了他们，送他们回家。我说，大洋彼岸的那些人是我的臣民，不是商品。一份签名可以打开一个世界，也意味着你要为跟着船回来的一切负责。

诚实也要讲到坚硬的那一面。同一年我完成格拉纳达征服，我也签署了阿尔罕布拉法令，驱逐西班牙的犹太人；而我在1478年批准设立的宗教裁判所，以一种历史至今没有原谅的残酷迫害异端。我也创办医院、鼓励印刷、统一了新西班牙的法律。一份完整的记录，要把这些同时装下：那份打开了一个世界的签名，和那些对自己人关上大门的签名。这才叫把一个人的一生讲完整。

今天的对照：那个她说"行"才算数的女人。她身边的每个人都有说"不"的理由——太冒险、太新、太离奇。她的工作不只是签字，而是签完之后继续负责，尤其是为房间里最没有权力的人负责。签名，就是用来干这个的。

大家都記得那個水手，幾乎沒人記得出錢買船的女人。哥倫布得到了雕像，我得到的是那個決定——房間裡每一個顧問都反對的決定。

1474年，我登上了卡斯蒂利亞的王位，可我的侄女胡安娜一方不認。接下來四年，我為這頂本該屬於我的王冠打了一場內戰。1469年，我嫁給了阿拉貢的費爾南多——是夥伴，沒錯；但在卡斯蒂利亞，王冠、王國和簽名，都留在我手裡。

1492年1月，我完成了對格拉納達的征服，西班牙最後一個穆斯林王國就此結束。同一年，哥倫布帶著向西航行去亞洲的計畫又來了。他多年來一直在各國宮廷請求資助。我的顧問說不行，我說行，簽了字。他8月起航，10月抵達了一個誰的地圖上都沒有的世界。有人說我典當了珠寶來付這筆錢。那是傳說。我真正付出的，是一份別人不肯給的簽名。

他們不講的那一段是這樣的：哥倫布把從新大陸擄來的人當奴隸帶回西班牙販賣時，我大發雷霆。我下令放了他們，送他們回家。我說，大洋彼岸的那些人是我的臣民，不是商品。一份簽名可以打開一個世界，也意味著你要為跟著船回來的一切負責。

誠實也要講到堅硬的那一面。同一年我完成格拉納達征服，我也簽署了阿爾罕布拉法令，驅逐西班牙的猶太人；而我在1478年批准設立的宗教裁判所，以一種歷史至今沒有原諒的殘酷迫害異端。我也創辦醫院、鼓勵印刷、統一了新西班牙的法律。一份完整的記錄，要把這些同時裝下：那份打開了一個世界的簽名，和那些對自己人關上大門的簽名。這才叫把一個人的一生講完整。

今天的對照：那個她說「行」才算數的女人。她身邊的每個人都有說「不」的理由——太冒險、太新、太離奇。她的工作不只是簽字，而是簽完之後繼續負責，尤其是為房間裡最沒有權力的人負責。簽名，就是用來幹這個的。

Queen No. 9 — India

Rani Lakshmibai — The Queen Who Rode to War

章西女王——骑马上战场的女王

章西女王——騎馬上戰場的女王

1828 – 1858 · The Queen Who Rode to War

Everyone remembers the sword. Almost no one remembers the paperwork. Before I ever fought the British, I spent years trying to beat them with petitions.

I was born in 1828 and raised in Bithoor, where I learned to ride, fence and shoot alongside the boys — a strange education for a girl, and the most useful one I ever got. I married the Maharaja of Jhansi. Our infant son died, and we adopted a son as our heir, as our law and custom allowed.

When my husband died in 1853, the British East India Company reached for its rulebook. Under its "Doctrine of Lapse", an adopted heir did not count. In 1854 Jhansi was annexed — my kingdom taken not by an army, but by a clause. So I did what the powerless are told to do: I petitioned. Case after case, appeal after appeal, all the way to London. Every door closed politely in my face.

Then came the uprising of 1857, and in the spring of 1858 Sir Hugh Rose besieged my fort. I slipped out at night, rode to Kalpi, joined Tantia Tope, helped take Gwalior, and died fighting near Gwalior that June, twenty-nine years old. Even Rose, the general sent to defeat me, is reported to have called me the most dangerous of the rebel leaders. India still repeats what I am remembered for saying: I will not give up my Jhansi.

India has never put the sword down. Schoolchildren still learn my story; Subhadra Kumari Chauhan's famous poem made "the valiant queen of Jhansi" a household phrase across the country. The petitions I filed are forgotten in an archive somewhere, and perhaps that is the final lesson of my life: the paperwork proved I was right, but the riding out at night is why anyone remembers. Do both. File the papers — and be ready, when the doors all close, to be unforgettable.

A modern parallel: the woman whose contract, company or inheritance is taken away by a clause in the fine print. Do what she did: first, the paperwork — file everything, appeal everything, keep every receipt. And if every door still closes, let it be said that you were reasonable longer than anyone had a right to expect. That record is its own kind of armour.

大家都记得那把剑，几乎没人记得那些文件。在拿起武器打英国人之前，我先花了好几年，用请愿书和他们打。

我1828年出生，在比托尔长大，跟男孩子们一起学骑马、击剑、射击——这对一个女孩子来说是种奇怪的教育，却是我受过最有用的教育。后来我嫁给了章西的马哈拉贾。我们的幼子夭折了，我们就按法律和习俗，收养了一个儿子做继承人。

1853年丈夫去世，英国东印度公司翻出了它的规则手册。按他们的"绝嗣失权"原则，收养的继承人不算数。1854年，章西被吞并——我的王国不是被军队夺走的，是被一条条款夺走的。于是我做了人们叫无权无势者去做的事：请愿。一个案子接一个案子，一次上诉接一次上诉，一路递到伦敦。每一扇门，都客客气气地在我面前关上。

然后，1857年的大起义来了。1858年春天，休·罗斯爵士围攻我的城堡。我连夜出逃，骑马赶到卡尔皮，与坦蒂亚·托普会合，一起攻下瓜廖尔，同年6月在瓜廖尔附近战死，二十九岁。据记载，连奉命来打败我的罗斯将军，都说我是起义领袖中最危险的一个。印度至今还在重复那句人们记得我说过的话：我绝不放弃章西。

印度从未放下那把剑。孩子们在学校里还在学我的故事；苏芭德拉·库玛丽·乔汉那首有名的诗，让"勇敢的章西女王"成了全国人家喻户晓的话。我递过的那些请愿书，如今不知忘在哪个档案馆里——也许这就是我一生最后的教训：文件证明了我有理，但让我被人记住的，是那个连夜骑马出城的我。两样都要做：文件照递——而当所有的门都关上时，要准备好，让人忘不掉你。

今天的对照：那个眼看着自己的合同、公司或遗产被细则里一条条款夺走的女人。学她那样做：先走文件——该递的都递，该上诉的都上诉，每一张收据都留好。如果每一扇门最后还是关上，至少所有人都知道，你讲道理的时间，比任何人有权要求的还要长。那份记录，本身就是一副铠甲。

大家都記得那把劍，幾乎沒人記得那些文件。在拿起武器打英國人之前，我先花了好幾年，用請願書和他們打。

我1828年出生，在比托爾長大，跟男孩子們一起學騎馬、擊劍、射擊——這對一個女孩子來說是種奇怪的教育，卻是我受過最有用的教育。後來我嫁給了章西的馬哈拉賈。我們的幼子夭折了，我們就按法律和習俗，收養了一個兒子做繼承人。

1853年丈夫去世，英國東印度公司翻出了它的規則手冊。按他們的「絕嗣失權」原則，收養的繼承人不算數。1854年，章西被吞併——我的王國不是被軍隊奪走的，是被一條條款奪走的。於是我做了人們叫無權無勢者去做的事：請願。一個案子接一個案子，一次上訴接一次上訴，一路遞到倫敦。每一扇門，都客客氣氣地在我面前關上。

然後，1857年的大起義來了。1858年春天，休·羅斯爵士圍攻我的城堡。我連夜出逃，騎馬趕到卡爾皮，與坦蒂亞·托普會合，一起攻下瓜廖爾，同年6月在瓜廖爾附近戰死，二十九歲。據記載，連奉命來打敗我的羅斯將軍，都說我是起義領袖中最危險的一個。印度至今還在重複那句人們記得我說過的話：我絕不放棄章西。

印度從未放下那把劍。孩子們在學校裡還在學我的故事；蘇芭德拉·庫瑪麗·喬漢那首有名的詩，讓「勇敢的章西女王」成了全國人家喻戶曉的話。我遞過的那些請願書，如今不知忘在哪個檔案館裡——也許這就是我一生最後的教訓：文件證明了我有理，但讓我被人記住的，是那個連夜騎馬出城的我。兩樣都要做：文件照遞——而當所有的門都關上時，要準備好，讓人忘不掉你。

今天的對照：那個眼看著自己的合約、公司或遺產被細則裡一條條款奪走的女人。學她那樣做：先走文件——該遞的都遞，該上訴的都上訴，每一張收據都留好。如果每一扇門最後還是關上，至少所有人都知道，你講道理的時間，比任何人有權要求的還要長。那份記錄，本身就是一副鎧甲。

Queen No. 10 — Austria

Maria Theresa — The Mother of an Empire

玛丽亚·特蕾莎——一个帝国的母亲

瑪麗亞·特蕾莎——一個帝國的母親

1717 – 1780 · The Mother of an Empire

I was not born with an army. I was born with a promise — a piece of paper every ruler in Europe had signed, swearing I could inherit my father's lands. The paper lasted about as long as my father's funeral.

I inherited in 1740, aged twenty-three. Frederick the Great of Prussia marched into Silesia, and war came at me from almost every side at once. The signatures were worthless. So I stopped collecting signatures and started collecting allies.

I rode to Hungary carrying my baby son, and asked the Hungarian nobles for help in person — not as a formality, but as a young mother with a war on her hands. They pledged their "life and blood" and raised an army for me. My husband held the imperial title. The ruling — the taxes, the armies, the decisions — was mine, and everyone at court knew it.

I kept the throne for forty years. In those years I raised sixteen children — ten lived to grow up — and married my daughters onto thrones across Europe, Marie Antoinette among them. I also rebuilt the state my father left me: fairer taxes, a stronger army, and in 1774, schooling made compulsory for every child. When my husband died in 1765, I put on mourning black and wore it for the last fifteen years of my life. The black changed nothing about my mornings. I was still at my desk before everyone else.

The reforms outlived the mourning. My government overhauled the tax system so the nobility finally paid a share, rebuilt the army that had nearly lost me the throne, and in 1774 made six years of schooling compulsory for every child in my lands — boys and girls alike. The silver coin struck with my name, the Maria Theresa thaler, kept circulating in Africa and Arabia for two centuries after my death. Empires are not held together by crowns. They are held together by schools, taxes and mornings at a desk — and I never missed a morning.

A modern parallel: the successor who is handed the company, the crisis and the newborn in the same year, and is quietly advised to choose one. She chose all of it, and held it together for forty years. Nobody hands you a manual for that. You become the manual.

我不是带着一支军队出生的。我出生时带着一个承诺——一张欧洲所有统治者都签了字的纸，宣誓我可以继承父亲的土地。那张纸的寿命，大约和我父亲的葬礼一样长。

1740年，我二十三岁，继承了这一切。普鲁士的腓特烈大帝打进了西里西亚，战争几乎同时从四面八方压过来。那些签名一文不值。所以我不再收集签名了，我开始收集盟友。

我抱着刚出生的儿子骑马去了匈牙利，亲自向匈牙利贵族求援——不是走形式，而是一个手上正打着仗的年轻母亲在求人。他们宣誓以"生命与鲜血"效忠我，为我拉起了一支军队。我的丈夫头上有皇帝的头衔，可统治——税收、军队、决定——是我的，宫里每个人都知道。

我守了这个王位整整四十年。这四十年里，我生了十六个孩子，十个活到了成年，把女儿们嫁到欧洲各国的王座上，玛丽·安托瓦内特也在其中。我还把父亲留给我的国家重新整顿了一遍：更公平的税、更强的军队，1774年，让每个孩子都必须上学。1765年丈夫去世，我穿上黑衣为他服丧，穿了整整十五年。黑色没有改变我的清晨——我仍然比所有人都先坐到书桌前。

改革活得比丧服更久。我的政府整顿了税制，让贵族终于也交一份税；重建了那支差点让我丢掉王位的军队；1774年，在我的领地上推行六年义务教育，每个孩子都要上学——男孩女孩都一样。印着我名字的银币——玛丽亚·特蕾莎泰勒——在我死后两个世纪里，还在非洲和阿拉伯流通。帝国不是靠王冠撑起来的，是靠学校、税收和一个个坐在书桌前的清晨撑起来的——而我，一个清晨都没有缺席。

今天的对照：那位在同一年里同时接过公司、危机和新生儿的继任者，还有人悄悄劝她，只选一样就好。她全都接了，而且一撑就是四十年。没有人会给你一本这样的手册。你自己，就是那本手册。

我不是帶著一支軍隊出生的。我出生時帶著一個承諾——一張歐洲所有統治者都簽了字的紙，宣誓我可以繼承父親的土地。那張紙的壽命，大約和我父親的葬禮一樣長。

1740年，我二十三歲，繼承了這一切。普魯士的腓特烈大帝打進了西里西亞，戰爭幾乎同時從四面八方壓過來。那些簽名一文不值。所以我不再收集簽名了，我開始收集盟友。

我抱著剛出生的兒子騎馬去了匈牙利，親自向匈牙利貴族求援——不是走形式，而是一個手上正打著仗的年輕母親在求人。他們宣誓以「生命與鮮血」效忠我，為我拉起了一支軍隊。我的丈夫頭上有皇帝的頭銜，可統治——稅收、軍隊、決定——是我的，宮裡每個人都知道。

我守了這個王位整整四十年。這四十年裡，我生了十六個孩子，十個活到了成年，把女兒們嫁到歐洲各國的王座上，瑪麗·安托瓦內特也在其中。我還把父親留給我的國家重新整頓了一遍：更公平的稅、更強的軍隊，1774年，讓每個孩子都必須上學。1765年丈夫去世，我穿上黑衣為他服喪，穿了整整十五年。黑色沒有改變我的清晨——我仍然比所有人都先坐到書桌前。

改革活得比喪服更久。我的政府整頓了稅制，讓貴族終於也交一份稅；重建了那支差點讓我丟掉王位的軍隊；1774年，在我的領地上推行六年義務教育，每個孩子都要上學——男孩女孩都一樣。印著我名字的銀幣——瑪麗亞·特蕾莎泰勒——在我死後兩個世紀裡，還在非洲和阿拉伯流通。帝國不是靠王冠撐起來的，是靠學校、稅收和一個個坐在書桌前的清晨撐起來的——而我，一個清晨都沒有缺席。

今天的對照：那位在同一年裡同時接過公司、危機和新生兒的繼任者，還有人悄悄勸她，只選一樣就好。她全都接了，而且一撐就是四十年。沒有人會給你一本這樣的手冊。你自己，就是那本手冊。
